arxiv-2203-16713.title: Wordle is N P - H A R D
arxiv-2203-16713.creator: Daniel Lokshtanov, Bernardo Subercaseaux
arxiv-2203-16713.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Daniel Lokshtanov, Bernardo Subercaseaux. Wordle is a single-player word-guessing game where the goal is to discover a secret word w w that has been chosen from a dictionary D D . In order to discover w w , the player can make at most ℓ \ell guesses, which must also be words from D D , all words in D D having the same length k k .

arxiv-2209-10560.title: Stabilizing fluctuating spin-triplet superconductivity in graphene via induced spin-orbit coupling
arxiv-2209-10560.creator: Jonathan B. Curtis, Nicholas R. Poniatowski, Yonglong Xie, Amir Yacoby, Eugene Demler, Prineha Narang
arxiv-2209-10560.description: Abstract A recent experiment showed that proximity induced Ising spin-orbit coupling enhances the spin-triplet superconductivity in Bernal bilayer graphene. Here, we show that, due to the nearly perfect spin rotation symmetry of graphene, the fluctuations of the spin orientation of the triplet order parameter suppress the superconducting transition to nearly zero temperature.

arxiv-2210-11064.title: Competitive Equilibrium for Dynamic Multi-Agent Systems: Social Shaping and Price Trajectories
arxiv-2210-11064.creator: Zeinab Salehi, Yijun Chen, Elizabeth L. Ratnam, Ian R. Petersen, Guodong Shi
arxiv-2210-11064.description: Abstract In this paper, we consider dynamic multi-agent systems (MAS) for decentralized resource allocation. The MAS operates at a competitive equilibrium to ensure supply and demand are balanced. First, we investigate the MAS over a finite horizon. The utility functions of agents are parameterized to incorporate individual preferences.

arxiv-2311-02635.title: Irreducible modules for map Heisenberg-Virasoro Lie algebras
arxiv-2311-02635.creator: Priyanshu Chakraborty
arxiv-2311-02635.description: Abstract . We study irreducible modules for map Heisenberg-Virasoro algebras. In particular, we give a complete classification of irreducible Harish-Chandra modules for map Heisenberg-Virasoro algebras. We will also classify non-weight irreducible modules for map Heisenberg-Virasoro algebras whose restriction on the degree zero part of the universal enveloping algebra of Witt algebra is free of rank 1.

arxiv-2405-00260.title: CREPE: Coordinate-Aware End-to-End Document Parser
arxiv-2405-00260.creator: Yamato Okamoto ∗ †, Youngmin Baek ∗ ‡, Geewook Kim, Ryota Nakao, DongHyun Kim, Moon Bin Yim, Seunghyun Park, Bado Lee
arxiv-2405-00260.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Yamato Okamoto ∗ †, Youngmin Baek ∗ ‡, Geewook Kim, Ryota Nakao, DongHyun Kim, Moon Bin Yim, Seunghyun Park, Bado Lee. In this study, we formulate an OCR-free sequence generation model for visual document understanding (VDU). Our model not only parses text from document images but also extracts the spatial coordinates of the text based on the multi-head architecture.

arxiv-2407-20053.title: Orca: Ocean Significant Wave Height Estimation with Spatio-temporally Aware Large Language Models
arxiv-2407-20053.creator: Zhe Li, Ronghui Xu, Jilin Hu, Zhong Peng, Xi Lu, Chenjuan Guo, Bin Yang
arxiv-2407-20053.description: Abstract . Significant wave height (SWH) is a vital metric in marine science, and accurate SWH estimation is crucial for various applications, e.g., marine energy development, fishery, early warning systems for potential risks, etc. Traditional SWH estimation methods that are based on numerical models and physical theories are hindered by computational inefficiencies.

arxiv-2409-02118.title: TSO : Self-Training with Scaled Preference Optimization
arxiv-2409-02118.creator: Kaihui Chen, Hao Yi, Qingyang Li, Tianyu Qi, Yulan Hu, Fuzheng Zhang, Yong Liu
arxiv-2409-02118.description: Abstract Enhancing the conformity of large language models (LLMs) to human preferences remains an ongoing research challenge. Recently, offline approaches such as Direct Preference Optimization (DPO) have gained prominence as attractive options due to offering effective improvement in simple, efficient, and stable without interactions with reward models.

arxiv-2504-10016.title: Quantifying Privacy Leakage in Split Inference via Fisher-Approximated Shannon Information Analysis
arxiv-2504-10016.creator: Ruijun Deng, Zhihui Lu, Qiang Duan
arxiv-2504-10016.description: Abstract Split inference (SI) partitions deep neural networks into distributed sub-models, enabling privacy-preserving collaborative learning. Nevertheless, it remains vulnerable to Data Reconstruction Attacks (DRAs), wherein adversaries exploit exposed smashed data to reconstruct raw inputs. Despite extensive research on adversarial attack-defense games, a shortfall remains in the fundamental analysis of privacy risks.

pmc-11433525.title: Risk Factors for Ovarian Cancer in South America: A Literature Review
pmc-11433525.creator: Sergio Jara-Rosales, Roxana González-Stegmaier, Elena S. Rotarou, Franz Villarroel-Espíndola
pmc-11433525.description: Background/Objectives: In 2020, ovarian cancer ranked fourth in global incidence among gynecological cancers and remains the deadliest cancer affecting women’s health. Survival rates are significantly higher when the disease is detected at early stages; however, the lack of effective early detection methods underscores the importance of identifying risk factors in order to implement preventive strategies.

pmc-11641052.title: Candidate SNP Markers Significantly Altering the Affinity of the TATA-Binding Protein for the Promoters of Human Genes Associated with Primary Open-Angle Glaucoma
pmc-11641052.creator: Karina Zolotareva, Polina A Dotsenko, Nikolay Podkolodnyy, Roman Ivanov, Aelita-Luiza Makarova, Irina Chadaeva, Anton Bogomolov, Pavel S Demenkov, Vladimir Ivanisenko, Dmitry Oshchepkov, Mikhail Ponomarenko, Hiroshi Tomita, Tsz Kin Ng
pmc-11641052.description: Primary open-angle glaucoma (POAG) is the most common form of glaucoma. This condition leads to optic nerve degeneration and eventually to blindness. Tobacco smoking, alcohol consumption, fast-food diets, obesity, heavy weight lifting, high-intensity physical exercises, and many other bad habits are lifestyle-related risk factors for POAG. By contrast, moderate-intensity aerobic exercise and the Mediterranean diet can alleviate POAG.

pmc-11646426.title: Title: A Qualitative Systematic Review of Parental Perceptions, Motivators, and Barriers to Management of Childhood Obesity
pmc-11646426.creator: Sarah Musa, Ayman Al-Dahshan, Vahe Kehyayan
pmc-11646426.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). BackgroundChildhood obesity is a global epidemic affecting millions worldwide. Children living with obesity face increased risks of health-related and psychosocial problems extending into adulthood. Parents and carers play a crucial role in cultivating healthy habits in their children. This review aims to synthesize qualitative research on parental perceptions, motivators, and barriers in managing childhood obesity and their views on weight management programs.MethodsThis systematic review was performed in accordance with the guidelines established by the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses.

pmc-11669991.title: Redox-Responsive Polymeric Nanogels as Efficient mRNA Delivery Vehicles in Caenorhabditis elegans
pmc-11669991.creator: Rupali Dabas, Alan Koh, David Carling, Nazila Kamaly, André E. X. Brown
pmc-11669991.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Efficient delivery of sensitive nucleic acid payloads, including mRNA, in Caenorhabditis elegans remains challenging, especially with traditional, labor-intensive transgenesis methods. We addressed these challenges using polymeric nanogels (NGs) as an advanced platform for mRNA delivery in C. These polymeric delivery vehicles can be engineered to suit desired applications owing to their chemical versatility, resulting from the ability to conjugate multiple functional groups onto the same backbone. Here, we validate the in vivo RNA delivery potential of redox-responsive NGs.

pmc-11704522.title: Malnutrition in adult patients treated with venoarterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation: A descriptive cohort study
pmc-11704522.creator: Stacy Pelekhaty, Julie Gessler, Devon Baer, Raymond Rector, Michael Plazak, Allison Bathula, Chris Wells, Aakash Shah, Alison Grazioli, Bradley Taylor, Bartley P Griffith, Joseph Rabin
pmc-11704522.description: ObjectiveTo evaluate malnutrition and its association with outcomes in adult patients requiring venoarterial (VA) extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO).MethodsPatients cannulated for VA ECMO between January 1, 2020, and January 1, 2023, were screened. Patients on ECMO for <48 hours or without a nutritional evaluation were excluded. Demographic and anthropometric data were collected retrospectively.

pmc-12567821.title: Hardware Implementation of Improved Oriented FAST and Rotated BRIEF-Simultaneous Localization and Mapping Version 2
pmc-12567821.creator: Ji-Long He, Ying-Hua Chen, Wenny Ramadha Putri, Chung-I Huang, Ming-Hsiang Su, Kuo-Chen Li, Jian-Hong Wang, Shih-Lun Chen, Yung-Hui Li, Jia-Ching Wang, Chris Rizos
pmc-12567821.description: The field of autonomous driving has seen continuous advances, yet achieving higher levels of automation in real-world applications remains challenging. A critical requirement for autonomous navigation is accurate map construction, particularly in novel and unstructured environments. In recent years, Simultaneous Localization and Mapping (SLAM) has evolved to support diverse sensor modalities, with some implementations incorporating machine learning to improve performance.

pmc-12682483.title: Dual-energy CT for distinguishing between T3 and T4 stages of locally advanced nasopharyngeal carcinoma
pmc-12682483.creator: Liyan Li, Xingye Yang, Yuhong Qin, Junli Liang, Li Jiang, Min Kang, Lina Chen, Zisan Zeng, Muliang Jiang, Bihong T Chen
pmc-12682483.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). BackgroundT staging is closely linked to the prognosis of patients with nasopharyngeal carcinoma (NPC), and dual-energy computed tomography (DECT) has a lot of promise for determining the degree of tumor invasion in head and neck cancers.

pmc-12707344.title: Review on the management of intra-abdominal candidiasis
pmc-12707344.creator: Pedro Puerta-Alcalde, Jesús Guinea, Emilio Maseda, Rafael Zaragoza
pmc-12707344.description: Intra-abdominal candidiasis, which includes Candida peritonitis and Candida produced intra-abdominal abscesses, accounts for 10-30% of all intra-abdominal infections diagnosed in the intensive care units. Intra-abdominal candidiasis is associated with longer hospital stay, and significantly higher morbidity and mortality. Although the management of invasive candidiasis has greatly improved in these past years, the optimal management of intra-abdominal candidiasis remains elusive.

pmc-12746242.title: Early prediction and warning of MODS following major trauma via identification of cytokine storm: A prospective cohort study
pmc-12746242.creator: Panpan Chang, Rui Li, Jiahe Wen, Guanjun Liu, Feifei Jin, Yongpei Yu, Yongzheng Li, Guang Zhang, Tianbing Wang
pmc-12746242.description: PurposeEarly mortality in major trauma has decreased, but MODS remains a leading cause of poor outcomes, driven by trauma-induced cytokine storms that exacerbate injuries and organ damage.MethodsThis prospective cohort study included 79 major trauma patients (ISS >15) treated in the National Center for Trauma Medicine, Peking University People's Hospital, from September 1, 2021, to July 31, 2023.

pmc-13063603.title: Prognostic stratification of cardiovascular risk and cardiac remodeling in prediabetes: a multimodal analysis comparing ADA and WHO/IEC diagnostic criteria
pmc-13063603.creator: Zhihao Zheng, Yanjun Song, Kongyong Cui, Jining He, Xiaohui Bian, Chenxi Song, Qiuting Dong, Chen Zhu, Rui Fu, Kefei Dou
pmc-13063603.description: BackgroundPrediabetes, an intermediate metabolic state preceding diabetes, independently accelerates cardiovascular pathology through dysglycemia-driven mechanisms. This study evaluates the heterogeneous cardiovascular risk stratification by directly comparing two major diagnostic criteria (ADA vs. WHO/IEC) and assesses the causal cardiovascular consequences of prediabetes, an area requiring further elucidation.

pmc-13234151.title: A 1-km Dataset of Water Consumption and Irrigation for Major Grain Crops in the Yellow River Basin Based on the Crop Water Production Function
pmc-13234151.creator: Zheng Wang, Changxiu Cheng, Kaixuan Dai, Zanmei Wei, Bin Li
pmc-13234151.description: Accurate estimation of crop water consumption and irrigation in the Yellow River Basin (YRB) is vital for water management and food security. Existing forward-logic methods (e.g., crop hydrological modeling method) fail to fully simulate key processes, leading to simulation biases. In contrast, the reverse-logic remote sensing inversion method covers full processes but is plagued by mixed-pixel effects.

pmc-13235123.title: Evaluation of alpha-gliadin celiac disease epitopes in some Aegilops species containing the D genome
pmc-13235123.creator: Rahman Ebrahimzadegan, Ghader Mirzaghaderi
pmc-13235123.description: Wheat gluten protein contains toxic peptides that trigger celiac disease in genetically susceptible individuals. These toxic peptides are primarily found in gliadin fractions, which are largely derived from the D subgenome of allohexaploid wheat. Aegilops species are valuable germplasm resources for wheat breeding.

pmc-13248758.title: Nanomicelle‐Based Multi‐mRNA Delivery Promotes Cardiac Repair After Myocardial Infarction
pmc-13248758.creator: Kazuma Handa, Takuji Kawamura, Yasunobu Mano, Hideyuki Nakanishi, Lisa Fujimura, Chie Kawai, Akima Harada, Kosuke Torigata, Kenji Miki, Keiji Itaka, Shigeru Miyagawa
pmc-13248758.description: Pathological remodeling after myocardial infarction (MI) involves multifactorial mechanisms, highlighting the need for combinatorial therapeutic strategies. Synthetic mRNAs offer design flexibility and represent a modality particularly suitable for such approaches. To investigate this, five genes (Hgf, Igf1, Pdgfb, Cxcl12, and Tgfβ1) were selected from a model in which extracellular vesicles secreted by human iPSC‐derived cardiomyocytes restored cardiac function.

uslaw-usc-t38-s5310.title: 38 U.S.C. § 5310 — Payment of benefits for month of death
uslaw-usc-t38-s5310.creator: United States Congress
uslaw-usc-t38-s5310.description: United States Code, Title 38 (Veterans’ Benefits); Part IV (General Administrative Provisions); Chapter 53 (Special Provisions Relating To Benefits). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. (a) In General.— (1) A surviving spouse of a veteran is entitled to a benefit for the month of the veteran’s death if— (A) at the time of the veteran’s death, the veteran was receiving compensation or pension.
